subject: Proper syntax for a multiple group Rasch calibration

messages.author: 61b685083edccef2
messages.subject: Proper syntax for a multiple group Rasch calibration
parts:
Hi Phil,

Congratulations on making a wonderful package in R. I am amazed at all the features you have built into mirt! 

I would like to run a multiple group calibration setting constraints on the slopes to 1. When I use the syntax below, it only constrains the first group's slopes to 1, but freely estimates the second group's slopes. 

mgrOneDRasch <- 'F1 = 1-27
START [Frm1,Frm2] = (1-27, a1, 1.0) 
FIXED [Frm1,Frm2] = (1-27, a1)'

mgr1D<- multipleGroup(data = dich2, model = oneDRasch, group = group, 
    invariance = c(itNames, "free_means", "free_var"),method = "MHRM")


In contrast, I seem to have no problem fitting a 1PL with this model syntax:

mgrOneD1pl <- 'F1 = 1-29
CONSTRAIN= (1-29, a1)'

Do you have any suggestions?

Thanks,

Garron

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Proper syntax for a multiple group Rasch calibration
parts:
Hi Garron,

Thanks for the kind words. mirt's been a fun project to work on over the years, though I feel my development with it has been slowing down now that my graduate student school years are over...

Your syntax generally looks good, and it's possible that there is a bug in the [] syntax form (it's very new, so I imagine situations like this would happen in the latest release). If possible, could you email me a short reproducible versions of this with some data? That way I can track it down and patch it more quickly.

For now though, I suppose I can offer this suggestion. If you pass itemtype = "Rasch" then the majority of the Rasch formulations will be imposed automatically. In other words, all the slopes will become fixed to 1 in all groups, and the hyper-parameter variances will also be freely estimated. HTH.

Phil
